extracted.intended_audience: Contracting officers and procurement/procurement-system personnel (Department of Defense / Navy) involved in A-76/CITA solicitations and cost comparisons
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative criteria for conducting Circular A-76 (CITA) solicitations, preparing and handling Government in-house cost estimates, performing cost comparisons between in-house and private-sector offers, and awarding or cancelling contracts under DOD/Navy procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three-year evaluation period advisory
rubrics_metrics.description: If the contract is to be for less than three years, bidders or offerers are to be advised that the three-year period is for evaluation purposes only and does not represent binding bids or offers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contract negotiator inserts 1, 2, or 3 as appropriate; the three-year projection period is the basis for the cost comparison unless modified by statute/regulation (e.g., Service Contract Act issues).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of cost comparison in solicitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Offerers are placed on notice that this solicitation is subject to a Government cost comparison to determine the economic feasibility of accomplishing the specified work in-house or by contract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Solicitation must state a cost-comparison will be conducted so offerers understand government in-house participation in evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sealed submission of Government in-house cost estimate
rubrics_metrics.description: The Government's in-house cost estimate, based upon the work statement set forth in this solicitation, shall be submitted to the contracting officer in a sealed envelope prior to the closing time for receipt of priced proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat the in-house estimate as a sealed 'proposal' and submit before closing to preserve integrity/confidentiality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public opening of in-house cost estimate with confidentiality of contractor prices
rubrics_metrics.description: At the conclusion of the negotiation process and after the most favorable offer has been determined, the contracting officer will set a time and place for the public opening of the Government's in-house cost estimate; no information relating to any contractor proposed prices will be provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contracting officer or representative will open and record the in-house estimate; interested parties may request copies of the in-house estimate.

rubrics_metrics.name: In-house estimate treated as a proposal under 'Late Proposals' provision
rubrics_metrics.description: For the purpose of the solicitation subparagraph 'Late Proposals, Modifications of Proposals, and Withdrawals of Proposals', the in-house cost estimate shall be considered a proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies procedural rules for timeliness and handling of the in-house estimate consistent with other proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Five work-day delay and appeals after opening
rubrics_metrics.description: Contract award shall not be made for at least five (5) work days after the time specified for opening of the in-house cost estimate to allow for review of the worksheet cost elements; any appeals regarding the cost comparison data shall be submitted in writing to the contracting officer within the five day work period after opening.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No action to complete the cost study until appeal decision is issued; ensures time for review and appeals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost comparison projection period (default three years)
rubrics_metrics.description: This cost comparison will be based on projections for a 3-year period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Cost Comparison Handbook originally used a 3-year period with government labor inflated at 4% per year; appropriateness of the inflation rate may be questionable given higher recent inflation; CO should consider current indices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include EEO, veterans preference, wage and fringe benefit clauses
rubrics_metrics.description: Circular requires inclusion of clauses relating to equal employment opportunity provisions, veterans preference and minimum wages and fringe benefits including OFPP Policy Letter No. 78-2 relating to 'wage busting' that would normally be included in most service contracts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also requires clause obligating contractor to give displaced employees the right of refusal for employment openings for which they may be qualified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local protective clauses for conversions
rubrics_metrics.description: Local clauses developed may include: requiring contractor cooperation in turnover/phase-in operations; contractor-developed strike contingency plan for Government review; reductions in contract price for nonavailability of operational assets or substandard performance; unbalanced bid evaluation clause; clause requiring contractor to use same number of personnel as proposed in Step One.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The legality/enforceability of some local clauses may be questionable; Contracting Officers have been including such clauses to protect Government interests in absence of explicit DAR coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of small and disadvantaged business set-asides
rubrics_metrics.description: Circular guidelines and current DOD and Navy directives encourage the use of small and disadvantaged businesses in acquisition of services in support of the CITA program; many Contracting Officers emphasize supporting this policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adherence creates issues (e.g., Section 8(a) procedures) that must be managed; negotiations with SBA can be complex and time-consuming.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion of SBA development monies from cost comparison
rubrics_metrics.description: SBA development monies will not be included in the cost comparison.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance reflects CNM direction: SBA development monies used by the contractor are excluded from the Government cost comparison calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of 8(a) set-asides and requirement for further solicitation
rubrics_metrics.description: CNM guidance: requirements processed under 8(a) procedures would require further solicitation under either Small Business Restricted Advertising or unrestricted solicitation if the in-house cost estimate was lower than the offer made by the 8(a) contractor; solicitations originally under competitive small business set-aside would not require further solicitation if Government in-house cost estimate was lower.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This clarifies when additional solicitation is necessary following 8(a) offers and cost comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opening in-house estimate for 8(a) set-aside but not making it public unless 8(a) offer is lower
rubrics_metrics.description: In the case of an 8(a) set-aside, the Government estimate will be opened but not made public unless the cost comparison indicates the 8(a) offer is lower; Contracting Officer must advise SBA, the 8(a) offerer, and union representatives of this procedure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some solicitations used a standard negotiation clause inconsistent with this CNM guidance; COs should follow latest authoritative guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection of solicitation methodology appropriate to circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: Solicitations and contracts may be negotiated pursuant to Section 8(a), utilize restricted small business advertising, or use Two-Step Formal Advertising; any method may be appropriate under different circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two-Step Formal Advertising can create problems (e.g., minimum manning disputes); where requirements can be clearly indicated, a performance oriented SOW and formal advertisement may be preferable to avoid problems created by technical proposals in step one.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid using contractor technical proposals to substitute for clear SOW/specifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Requesting contractor technical proposals should not be used as a crutch to offset the lack of clear and accurate specifications regarding performance of the desired service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clear performance-oriented SOWs and surveillance plans allow performance deductions to be based on standards rather than proposed staffing levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum manning levels proposed in step-one may be enforceable issue
rubrics_metrics.description: If a contractor refuses to provide the minimum manning levels indicated in his technical proposal submitted in step one, disputes may arise (example where CO withheld payment citing Inspection of Services Clause).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whether contractor must man to proposed levels is likely a legal question; COs should be aware of the risk of such disputes when using Two-Step procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incentive-type contracts and Formal Advertising exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: The use of incentive type contracts for conversions necessitates the use of one of the DAR exceptions to Formal Advertising; it may be difficult to justify negotiated procurement as necessary because it would be less costly or impractical to secure required supplies/services without negotiation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incentive pricing arrangements may be more applicable to large, complex, new starts than to individual conversions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of pre-priced options to deter buy-ins and lengthen comparison base
rubrics_metrics.description: Revised Circular recommends solicitations should provide for pre-priced options for out-year performance to prevent potential buy-ins and provide a broader period (e.g., three years) on which to base the cost comparison.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advantages include continuity of performance and reduced disruption; conflicts exist with DAR preference for resolicitation of annual requirements when services are readily available on the open market.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service Contract Act impact requires one-year cost comparison where applicable
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the Service Contract Act mandates redetermination of labor rates for covered contractor employees, the cost comparison will be made for one year only; pre-priced options still required where SCA not applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NAVSUP revised Cost Comparison Handbook to reflect this change for solicitations released after October 1, 1979; COs must know applicability of SCA to the requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contracting officer must lead solicitation/evaluation cycle activities and explain cost procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: During the solicitation/evaluation cycle the Contracting Officer conducts prebid or preproposal conferences, negotiations if necessary, and evaluation of private sector responses; COs are responsible for explaining cost procedures to be applied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CO must have more than passing familiarity with procedures for calculating the in-house cost estimate and how it will be compared to industry offers; check message traffic daily for policy changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prebid/preproposal conference content and site visit control
rubrics_metrics.description: Preproposal memorandums should explain in detail the cost differentials depending on conversion vs new start; if the service results in a product, a Government-produced sample should be available; site visits may be required and must be controlled to avoid informal communications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarify Bid/Performance Bonds treatment (Gov estimate excludes similar amount) and whether existing personnel can be used by contractor; avoid offerers obtaining additional/contradictory info outside controlled amending process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat Government like other offerer when amendments/clarifications occur
rubrics_metrics.description: If solicitation amendments are required, the Government should be treated exactly as another offerer; procedures should ensure Task Group Chairperson is included in distribution for all amendments and clarifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referrals for clarifications must go through the CO to the Task Group Chairperson; CO must ensure the in-house estimate is updated to reflect changes to preserve integrity of comparison.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and conditions for price competition (DAR four conditions)
rubrics_metrics.description: DAR states that for price competition to exist four conditions must be met: (1) at least two responsible offerors, (2) who can satisfy the requirements, (3) independently contend for a contract to be awarded to the responsive, responsible offeror submitting the lowest evaluated price, (4) by submitting priced offers responsive to expressed requirements of the solicitation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using this definition, the Government can be characterized as an offeror in CITA procurements and considered an independent seller for price-competition purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determine and enter 'contract price' on cost comparison form (Line 10)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Contracting Officer must determine the low contract price and enter the 'Contract Price' on line 10 of the cost comparison form; combined with the in-house estimate, this forms the basis for the cost comparison.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determination varies by contract pricing arrangement; COs need guidance/methodologies for incentive, cost-reimbursement, and time-and-materials contracts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of firm fixed-price contracts and payment discounts
rubrics_metrics.description: Firm fixed-price arrangements: the price of the low offerer will be entered as the contract price.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Cost Comparison Handbook is silent as to whether to include payment discounts (e.g., early payment) — recommendations have been made to include them because they reduce total Government costs and are used as evaluation criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of fixed-price with economic price adjustments and other fixed-price variants
rubrics_metrics.description: Fixed-Price Contracts with Economic Price Adjustments are not mentioned in the handbook; other variants (FP Incentive - successive targets, FP with redetermination retroactive/prospective) are not covered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: COs may need to use judgment, recent price trends, indices, or other methodologies to determine a fair and reasonable price to enter on the form; some variants (e.g., redetermination-retroactive) may be incompatible with cost comparison.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate fixed-price incentive arrangements based on target price
rubrics_metrics.description: Fixed-Price Incentive pricing arrangements (e.g., FPIF) are to be evaluated based on the target price.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Earlier debates existed over using the ceiling rather than the target price; unions and some memos argued for using maximum potential liability (ceiling), but current guidance uses the target.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost reimbursement contract evaluation and use of auditors
rubrics_metrics.description: Cost Reimbursement Contracts must be subjected to meticulous technical and cost evaluation to assure estimated costs are neither over- nor under-estimated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Auditors should be requested to check offerors' estimates for realism; COs must ensure estimates are fair and reasonable and adjust/negotiated as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: What to enter for CPFF/CPIF/CPAF contracts
rubrics_metrics.description: CPFF: sum of total estimated costs and fixed fee would be entered; CPIF: target cost combined with target fee would be used; CPAF: the fee portion commensurate with the performance level attributed to Government employees will be estimated and included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Handbook gives limited guidance; CO must exercise informed independent judgment, consult estimators/functional managers to determine appropriate fee portion for CPAF based on comparable performance levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of Time-and-Materials and Labor-Hour contracts
rubrics_metrics.description: For T&M or Labor-Hour contracts the total estimated cost of performance may be calculated and entered or comparable rates may be developed and the cost comparison conducted on the basis of rates rather than total costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research did not reveal many instances of using rate-based comparisons; COs may select method that provides equitable comparison.

rubrics_metrics.name: Necessity to evaluate cost realism and adjust contractor offers upward if needed
rubrics_metrics.description: The Handbook emphasizes the necessity for evaluating cost realism; upward price revisions to contractor offers may need to be negotiated to ensure equity in the cost comparison.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typical price negotiation yields a Government position lower than contractor's offer; COs must ensure contractor estimates are realistic and adjust if unrealistic.

rubrics_metrics.name: CO responsibility and familiarity with methodologies for determining contract price
rubrics_metrics.description: Determination of the 'contract price' to be entered on the cost comparison form may represent one of the most important responsibilities directly attributable to the Contracting Officer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many contracting personnel were not aware of their total responsibilities or familiar with methodologies; COs should seek training and consult handbooks/auditors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition of award adjustments as 'award factors' not evaluation factors
rubrics_metrics.description: At bid opening or upon completion of negotiations adjustments will be made to reflect other Government costs incurred only if a contract is awarded (e.g., transportation, contract administration, Government furnished materials/supplies, contractor use of Government-owned equipment/facilities, standby maintenance costs, Government personnel termination costs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These costs are award factors (not used to determine offeror's grasp or expertise) and should be addressed in award cycle processing rather than treated as evaluation factors during proposal evaluation.
